title: Strongly Misaligned Triple System in SR 24 Revealed by ALMA
question: Are the disks of the young triple system SR24 misaligned, and what are their masses, kinematics and the extended gas structures around them?

data.sensitivity: continuum rms 44 uJy/beam; C18O 1.2 mJy/beam per 1.35 km/s; 12CO 4.6 (taper) and 5.2 mJy/beam per 0.6 km/s

evidence.quote: a dust opacity of 1.1 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ at 1.3 mm appropriate for dust with thin ice mantles
an opacity spectral index with an exponent $\beta=0.4$ for both sources

what.value: Binary SR24Nb/Nc orbit and mass of close binary

evidence.quote: is in good agreement with the total mass of the close binary system

recipe.goal: Image continuum and measure disk properties
recipe.method: Self-calibrated natural-weighted 1.3 mm image; source flux, size, PA from deconvolved ellipse; inclination = arccos(Rmin/Rmaj)

key_parameters: kappa=1.1 cm2/g at 1.3 mm, beta=0.4, T_dust=30 K

recipe.goal: Characterize 12CO disk kinematics and SR24N dynamical mass
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fits to moment 0, PV diagrams with Keplerian curves, M=0.00121*(dv/2)^2*r

recipe.goal: Fit SR24S C18O velocity cube with kinematic model
recipe.method: Thin rotating, accreting disk with tapered power-law surface density, r^-0.5 rotation and infall, no radiative transfer; 9 free parameters; M=v_rot^2 r/G

recipe.goal: Determine tilt/sense of rotation and misalignment angle
recipe.method: PV cuts perpendicular to major axis compared with synthetic infall models; angle via cosΔ=cos i1 cos i2+sin i1 sin i2 cos(PA1-PA2)
assumptions: SR24N disk rotates in same sense as the close binary; infall rather than outflow

recipe.goal: Mass of extended gas from SMA 12CO
recipe.method: LTE optically thin mass formula with Tex=30 K, X_CO/X_H2=1e-4, d=0.12 kpc

evidence.quote: for SR24S we obtain a mass of 0.025$\pm0.007$ $M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$

evidence.loc: 3.3 Simple modeling of the SR24S disk kinematics

evidence.quote: The resulting mass, 0.8 $M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$, is in good agreement

answer_key.quantity: Angle between disk angular momentum vectors

evidence.quote: we derive an angle between the angular momentum vectors of the two disks[^8] of $108\ensuremath{^\circ}\pm25\ensuremath{^\circ}$

not_stated_but_needed: CASA version and whether the pipeline or manual calibration was used
uv-taper value and clean parameters (threshold, niter, cell, image size)
line-free channels and continuum subtraction method
how the 12CO disk velocity ranges and 2D Gaussian fits were done
how errors on inclination and PA were propagated
score_reason: Public data and a clear simple recipe, but clean/selfcal parameters and fitting code details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric results (fluxes, masses, fitted parameters), moderately complete recipe.
